A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ChartMoE and its alignment dataset. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison despite the revised title and expanded presentation.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, architecture and training ablations, expert-routing analyses, and chart-editing demonstrations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds general VQA evaluations, further controls, dataset quality assessment, and additional comparative analyses.

M1.justification: The architecture, routing equations, expert initialization tasks, three-stage training, and PoT inference are retained. v2 explicitly documents omission of balancing/router z-losses; v1 did not specify using them, so this disclosure does not establish a changed training objective.

E1.justification: v2 adds quantitative evaluation on MME and MMBench, extending coverage to general visual perception and reasoning beyond chart tasks and routing visualizations. The original chart benchmarks and training sources remain; 'nearly 1 million' replaces 'over 900K' without changing Table 1's dataset counts.

E2.justification: v2 introduces Qwen-2.5 and GPT-4O comparisons in chart-editing demonstrations, adds the Random Align control in Table 5, and compares against Direct SFT in general VQA evaluations. Comparator membership in the original main benchmark tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include a dense Direct SFT control using Table 1's data, LLaVA-v1.5-7B experiments using 10% of the alignment data plus ChartQA training, and a 200-quadruple quality audit with binary GPT-4o ratings and at least three human reviewers per item. The original ChartMoE training recipe and benchmark splits are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of general-capability retention, balancing/router-loss effects, random alignment, transfer to another backbone, dataset quality, and numeric versus non-numeric ChartQA errors. Appendix editing demonstrations are revised into comparative case studies. Existing routing analyses are retained, with an additional loss-condition panel in Figure 10.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated training runs, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The new audit's sample size and reviewer counts describe its evaluation design without adding uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Original main benchmark scores remain unchanged, including ChartMoE+PoT's 84.64% on ChartQA and ChartMoE's 51.67% on ChartBench. Added results include Random Align's 75.60%, 78.28% with bz-loss versus 78.76% without it, general VQA scores, dataset quality ratings, Tables 10-11, and comparative editing outcomes. These are additional results, not version-to-version benchmark gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1-3 retain the same visual encoding, sparse expert routing, and language-model output definitions. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The four principal contributions and headline ChartQA claim remain. v2 reframes the motivation around preserving general capabilities and adds the introductory claim that omitting expert-balancing loss improves performance, without replacing the central method or dataset contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting general-capability retention to the vanilla expert and unfavorable balancing-loss effects to unequal visual-token distributions. Appendix D.4 introduces specific limitations: adaptation beyond charts requires new alignment tasks, and adding experts requires router retraining. The earlier string-matching caveat is retained and expanded through the error analysis.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly documents source selection, overlap removal, balanced sampling, JSON attributes, code generation, and rendering filters for the existing dataset. Appendix D.1 adds parameter, latency, and memory measurements; Table 9's hyperparameters remain unchanged. The v1 homepage link disappears, while v2 promises future dataset/checkpoint releases through GitHub and Hugging Face without establishing their availability.

R1.justification: Although Section 2 is largely retained, Appendix D.1 substantially expands positioning against MoE-LLaVA, DeepSeek-VL, and CuMo, explicitly claiming novelty in applying MoE exclusively to the connector with limited overhead. v2 also adds references supporting the general VQA evaluations and new editing comparators.

P1.justification: The introduction and alignment-task explanations are substantially rewritten. v2 retitles the paper, integrates the former Section 5.4 into Section 5.3, expands Appendix C into five subsections, introduces a discussion appendix, moves editing material from D to E, and adds reproducibility and acknowledgment sections.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 7-9 and Tables 10-11, extends the appendix routing figure with a loss-condition panel, and rebuilds editing demonstrations as comparative displays with reference tables. Existing benchmark and ablation tables are regrouped and relocated, and the document adopts conference typography and headers.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for preserving general capabilities through Figures 7-8 and for dataset quality through Appendix C.4, addressing properties that v1 largely asserted or left unvalidated. Expanded construction details and explicit adaptation limitations also improve assessability. Table 11 introduces an unresolved inconsistency: ChartMoE's 74.80% and 91.84% split averages imply 83.32%, not its listed 84.64%. This weakens that analysis, but the broader validation and transparency gains provide a substantial net improvement.
